title: Sequential and sectionwise coefficient localization agree
statement: Let C be a small site with topology J, R a sheaf of commutative rings, U an object and f in R(U). On C/U let R_U be the restricted ring sheaf. The sequential colimit of copies of R_U with transition multiplication by the restricted section f [def-weil-pbc-ringed-site-section-localization] is isomorphic, as an R_U-module sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], to the sheafification of the presheaf V ↦ R_U(V)[1/f|V], with localization-lift restriction maps [def-weil-pbc-ringed-section-localization]. No hypothesis on f, R or J beyond those stated is imposed.

proof.text: At an object V of the slice send a at stage n to a/f_V^n in the actual localization. The transition relation is respected. Every fraction has such a representative; if two fractions agree, a further power of f_V kills the difference of their cross-multiplied numerators, giving equality at a common later stage. Thus this cocone is a colimit in modules. The argument includes zero and nilpotent f and the zero ring.

source.place: Tags 0997 and 099C, as expanded by the stated construction comparisons

proof.text: Localization lifts send numerator and inverted f to their restrictions, so the fraction maps commute with all restriction maps. Pointwise colimit universal properties assemble to the presheaf colimit. Apply the left-adjoint module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], which preserves colimits. Its counit identifies the sheafified unit with the original unit, giving the asserted sheaf isomorphism.

lean.statement:
theorem sectionLocalization_sequence_iso
    {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
    (R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u}) (U : C) (f : R.obj.obj (op U)) :
    Nonempty
      (ringedSiteSectionLocalization ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj R)
        U f ≅ ringedSectionLocalization (R.over U) (ringedSliceSection R U f))
